newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: LATE TRADES UP PERSETEL PROFURN, BARLOWS.
newsitem.headline: LATE TRADES UP PERSETEL PROFURN, BARLOWS.

text.p: Volumes in South Africa's information technology (IT) firm Persetel continued to surge on Tuesday after a move to merge with Q-Data to create a 12 billion rand company, dealers said.
Also basking under heavy volumes were industrial firm Barlows and furniture group Protea Furnishers (Profurn) following deals carried over from Monday by various stockbroking firms.
"These were all late trades and I think there is still interest in Persetel over the Q-Data merger move," one dealer at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) said.
In Persetel around 1.5 million shares worth around 55.6 million rand had exchanged hands within the first half hour of trade, while in Barlows there were over 600,000 shares worth 36.1 million rand.
Barlows was up 50 cents at 60.25 rand while Persetel added 25 cents to 36.25 rand.
Profurn saw volumes of just over 827,000 valued at 2.2 million rand.
Buying in Persetel, Profurn and Barlows had accounted for most of Monday's market turnover, the dealers added.
Persetel said last Thursday it would buy all of Q-Data's businesses and merge with their own.
The merged company, to be called Persetel Q-Data (PQ) Holdings, would have an expected market capitalisation of 12 billion rand, making it the 22nd largest company on the JSE.
